editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article text and Rules of Golf text are never copied; rules and news are explained in Swoon'd's own words with rule numbers and links to the original.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: She can follow a round or a golf broadcast, understand par, penalties, formats and the big events, ask a couple of good questions about a shot, a putt or a course, and say 'okay, I get why you love this' without faking it.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Procedural or original illustrations only (license original-swoond); no third-party player, event or course photography without a written license; famous-hole lessons use original schematics.
Original foley or synthesised strike and putt sounds only; no broadcast, commentary or crowd audio.

PGA TOUR, LPGA, DP World Tour, LIV Golf, R&A, USGA, PGA of America, Ryder Cup, Solheim Cup, Presidents Cup, Masters, Augusta National, equipment brands and team marks are trademarks: text mentions and link-outs only, no logos or event artwork without permission.
No embedded broadcast video; deep-link to official streams.
Never copy publisher text or Rules of Golf text; paraphrase with rule numbers and link.

Live scores only via a licensed provider or official partnership; no unofficial or reverse-engineered tour or media endpoints; TheSportsDB only after golf coverage and terms are confirmed; OpenStreetMap needs ODbL attribution.
Names as facts only; no likeness, endorsement implication, or fabricated quotes.
No betting odds, tips or gambling promotion; friendly formats (skins, Nassau) are explained as social games only.

safetyConstraints: On-course safety guidance stays conservative and generic: shout 'Fore!' and stay aware of golf balls; when the course sounds its lightning warning or thunder is heard, leave the course and follow its procedure; never shelter under a tree or hold a club aloft.
Heat, sun, hydration, cart and injury content stays generic (warm up, stay hydrated, stop if it hurts, see a professional); no medical claims.
Rules and etiquette scenarios teach honesty, de-escalation and asking an official; never coach confrontation, cheating or fudged scores.
Swoon'd builds appreciation, not a substitute for lessons, club fitting or fitness training; never encourage the learner to fake a skill level or expertise with the person they care about.
